transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Narang (Head of ML, Cobalt), Evan Soto (Platform Eng), Rafael Martinez (CTO)

Auto-generated summary: kickoff for POC timeline and milestones, confirm access, run benchmarks, define success gates.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, will kick off. Uh, quick intro round please.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, Priya here. Head of ML at Cobalt Analytics. We're really excited to scope this POC — we've got a few production use cases to validate.
[00:28] Evan: Evan, platform eng, I'll own the infra side and access.
[00:33] Rafael: Rafael, CTO, dropping in for timelines and exec alignment.
[00:38] Maya: Great, Liam and I will run through the recommended timeline and benchmarks, then talk security and access. Goal is to leave with concrete owners and dates.
[00:50] Liam: Quick note: we'll propose both hosted and Redwood Dedicated paths for the POC but focus on the one that matches your success criteria.
[01:02] Priya: Our must-haves — latency p95 under 450ms for real-time features, and cost no more than 50% above our current infra unit cost. Also model quality parity on the QA test set.
[01:18] Maya: Perfect, we should codify those as the success matrix. We'll capture latency, cost per 1k tokens, and end-to-end correctness on the sample prompt set.
[01:30] Evan: On infra, we'll need VPC peering or an S3 transfer pattern. Can you support Private deployment? We might need Private VPC for PHI-ish data.
[01:44] Liam: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem connectors, and we can run a Dedicated pool in your region. For the POC we usually start with hosted for speed, then move to a dedicated spin-up if you need isolation.
[02:00] Rafael: What's the expected time to get Dedicated capacity? If exec likes results we might want to flip quickly.
[02:07] Maya: Typical spin-up is 2-3 weeks for Dedicated after the contract, but for the POC we can provision a dedicated trial node in about a week with approvals.
[02:20] Priya: Ok, good. For benchmarks, we have three workload patterns: 1) real-time shorter prompts p95 ~300-600ms, 2) batch re-rank jobs, and 3) long-context summarization to 4k tokens. We need the POC to cover all three.
[02:38] Liam: That's helpful. We'll provide benchmark scripts that exercise those: continuous qps, batching scenarios, and a long-context path; include KV cache behavior too.
[02:48] Evan: Can Redwood's runtime handle our long-context use cases without exploding cost? We use quantized weights and some pruning.
[02:55] Liam: We have quantization profiles and kernel selections; we'll recommend a quantized 4-bit run for cost, and an FP16 path for quality if needed. Expect trade-offs — we'll measure perplexity/quality and tokens/sec.
[03:12] Maya: Let's walk through milestone timing. Proposed POC timeline:
  - Week 0 (this week): kickoff, access & security docs exchanged, seed dataset shared.
  - Week 1: Access enabled, initial baseline runs on hosted, smoke tests.
  - Week 2: Full benchmark runs and tuning (batch sizes, cache configs).
  - Week 3: Mid-point technical review — validate gates, iterate on configs.
  - Week 4: Final benchmark, exec readout prep, deliverables and exec summary.
[03:49] Rafael: Exec readout in 4 weeks seems tight; can we make it 8 weeks to include canary in prod?
[03:55] Priya: Yeah, I think 8 weeks is better for our org — need time for stakeholder reviews.
[04:01] Maya: We can do an 8-week timetable: mid-point at week 3-4, technical readout at week 6, exec readout at week 8. We'll capture gates at each checkpoint.
[04:12] Liam: Gate definitions: access readiness, benchmark completion with pass/fail on success matrix, and security sign-off. Each gate has owners.
[04:20] Evan: For access, what do you need exactly? S3 read-only? IAM roles? VPC peering?
[04:27] Liam: For hosted benchmarks S3 presigned URLs are enough. For Private/Dedicated we'll ask for VPC peering details and a list of subnets. We'll send a minimal network diagram.
[04:36] Priya: Security questions: Are audit logs available? KMS for key management? SOC2 scope?
[04:41] Maya: Yes — we have audit logs, KMS integrations, and a SOC2 report. We'll attach the latest docs; note that PII/PHI handling depends on deployment mode (hosted vs private).
[04:56] Rafael: Any blockers on data residency? We need EU region for some subsets.
[05:02] Liam: We can run in EU region clusters; we'll map latency expectations per region in the benchmark.
[05:09] Priya: About cost — can you show cost per 1k tokens for the different quantization and batch configs?
[05:16] Maya: Yes, Liam will produce a cost model with sensitivity to batch sizes and kv cache hit rates.
[05:23] Liam: On the benchmark scripts: we'll push a GitHub repo with runner, seed prompts, and expected metrics. We'll include 1k-token mixes and 10k-token long-context cases. Also, we'll instrument token-level timing so you can map p50/p95.
[05:40] Priya: Great. For success criteria thresholds, I'll draft a table but preliminarily: latency p95 < 450ms, accuracy within 2% F1 vs baseline, cost <= 1.5x current.
[05:55] Maya: That works. We'll translate that to pass/fail checks in the benchmark harness.
[06:02] Evan: On tooling, do you support tracing hooks to link requests back to our logs?
[06:07] Liam: Yes, tracing headers and request IDs can be propagated; we'll share the spec.
[06:12] Priya: Any competitors we should consider? We're still evaluating Anthropic and our internal infra.
[06:18] Maya: Noted. We'll emphasize Redwood's production controls and cost levers.
[06:25] Rafael: For the mid-point review who should attend? Engineering leads and maybe a solutions architect from our side.
[06:32] Maya: Recommended: AE, SE, your Head of ML, platform eng, and a product owner. We'll set a 60-minute slot.
[06:39] Priya: Ok. One logistical question: do you need sample PII data for quality tests? We can't share real PII.
[06:45] Liam: We can use synthetic or redacted datasets. The benchmark harness supports masking.
[06:51] Maya: Let's confirm immediate action items — we'll send SOC2 and network diagram by tomorrow, Liam will upload benchmark repo, Priya/Evan will provide sample prompts and S3 access.
[07:01] Evan: I'll work on the IAM policy and share by Friday.
[07:06] Priya: I'll draft the success criteria table and circulate.
[07:10] Rafael: Once we have mid-point results, we'll decide whether to convert to Dedicated and start contracting.
[07:16] Maya: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[07:19] Priya: One: can Redwood simulate our exact peak load? We might have spikes to 250 qps.
[07:26] Liam: Yes, the benchmark runner can spike load; we'll schedule a stress window and measure tail latency.
[07:34] Maya: Great. Recap of next steps: (1) Redwood send security + network docs; (2) Redwood send benchmark scripts and cost model; (3) Cobalt share sample prompts and access; (4) schedule mid-point and exec readout. We'll follow up with calendar invites.
[07:52] Rafael: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the POC.
[07:56] Maya: Thanks all, talk soon.

Auto-generated action items (captured above): Maya to send docs, Liam to share repo and scripts, Evan & Priya to provide access and success criteria.

End of transcript.
